The slot board took a fresh sheet every shift, and Vance had learned to read it from the far
end of the gallery by the shape of the block rather than by the words. Today's block was
short. Short meant refusals.

She went down past the exchanger trunks, which ran hot enough to walk wide of, and stood in
front of the board long enough to be seen there. The sealing order was pinned at the top
under co-op letterhead, three lines and a date. Below it, in the same hand, the shift's soak
slots. None of them were hers.

Behind the board the gallery ran on to the soak lock, and past the lock six hours of cold
soak, and past that the water she had been down four hundred times. The board had never been
built to care.
